newsitem.title: CANADA: Pools seek competition ruling on deal-MPE.
newsitem.headline: Pools seek competition ruling on deal-MPE.

text.p: Two grain handling firms that dropped their hostile takeover bid for rival United Grain Growers Ltd said Wednesday they want a Competition Bureau ruling to determine whether any such mergers would be allowed, Manitoba Pool Elevators lawyer Anders Bruun said.

"One of the barriers to the two Pools doing something in conjunction with UGG is the competition issue," Bruun told Reuters. "We've put information before the Competition Bureau and we're asking them to proceed so we can get some indication to see what the competition issues might be if we were to do something following discussion with UGG or otherwise."

MPE and Alberta Wheat Pool on February 20 launched a C$13.75 a share hostile bid for UGG but dropped the C$172 million offer March 18 after a Manitoba court ruled UGG's poison pill had been triggered.
The Pools jointly own 1,872,200 limited voting common UGG shares, or about 14.98 percent of UGG stock.

UGG's directors Friday authorized management to continue talks with firms that came forward during the takeover attempt "if the talks could lead to an appropriate transaction that would enhance shareholder value."
UGG said it had not spoken with the Pools since March 18.
"Basically, we're not going to close any doors that would enhance shareholder value," UGG president and chairman Ted Allen told Reuters.
The Pools were studying at least four investment choices, one of them involving UGG, Bruun said.
"It's our view that all of our options remain open, including the option involving transactions with UGG," Bruun said.
"There are a number of other very solid options we're looking at but we want to make sure that option remains an open and viable one," he added.
